bug.title: A negative retry-after makes post_json retry immediately instead of backing off on the exponential ladder
bug.symptoms: providers._live_http._retry_after_seconds("-5") answers 0.0, because it returns max(0.0, seconds). post_json then retries a 429 carrying retry-after: -5 after sleep(0.0). A vendor or proxy that keeps sending a negative value gets max_attempts requests in a burst with no backoff. bug_spec_live_providers.xml bug 1 specified the opposite: "A retry-after that is not a finite non-negative number (nan, an HTTP date, empty) falls back to the exponential ladder." RFC 9110 section 10.2.3 defines Retry-After delay-seconds as a non-negative integer, so a negative value is malformed. It is not a request to retry now.
bug.reproduction_steps: Call post_json("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", {}, {}, allowed_hosts={"api.anthropic.com"}, transport=T, sleep=S), where T answers (429, {"retry-after": "-5"}, b"{}") first and (200, {}, b'{"ok": 1}') second. S records 0.0, where the ladder's first wait (1 s plus jitter) was expected.
bug.expected: _retry_after_seconds answers None for any negative value (for example "-5", "-0.5" and "-inf"), exactly as it does for nan, an HTTP date and an empty value. post_json then waits on the exponential ladder (1, 2, 4 s plus jitter, capped by MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS). - "0" stays a valid wait of 0.0, because zero is non-negative. - Every other retry-after behaviour is unchanged: the ceiling refusal above 60 s (including inf), honouring finite values at or below 60, and the ladder for nan and dates. - The docstring sentence "A negative delta clamps to zero" is replaced by one stating that a negative delta is malformed and falls back to the ladder. - Tests cover "-5", "-0.5" and "-inf" (ladder, sleep at least 1.0), and "0" (sleep 0.0), with an injected sleep that records its argument.
bug.actual: Root cause: packages/providers/src/providers/_live_http.py, _retry_after_seconds ends `return max(0.0, seconds)`, which clamps negatives to zero instead of rejecting them as malformed.
bug.constraints: No network access and no real credential in any test No third-party dependency; pyproject.toml and uv.lock are not edited No file outside the two listed is edited The host guard, the secret scrubbing, the retryable status set, the 4xx no-retry rule and the retry-after ceiling keep their behaviour and tests Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
